title: Per-model quant defaults: curation, calibration harness, and safety matrix
creator: Avery Kim
description: Create and publish per-model default quantization profiles in the model catalog, backed by an automated calibration and validation pipeline. Deliverables: (1) curated default profile (FP8/INT8/FP16 fallback) for each model in the catalog, (2) a repeatable calibration harness that produces calibration artifacts and accuracy deltas, (3) a safety matrix with enforced guardrails and rollback rules, and (4) console fields for displaying the recommended default and the confidence band. This ticket coordinates engineering work for catalog metadata, runtime fallbacks, CI validation, and canary rollout plan.
acceptance_criteria: Each supported model in the staging catalog has a default quant profile (one of: fp8_dynamic, int8_static, fp16) recorded as model_catalog.quant_default

Calibration harness runs end-to-end for a new model in under 90 minutes on our calibration runner and produces a reproducible artifact (calibration table + clipping params + validation report), stored at s3://redwood-quant/calibrations/<model>/<sha>.tar.gz

Automatic validation compares baseline (FP16) vs quantized model on a standardized eval set; policy enforces max allowed accuracy delta: <=1.0% absolute for classification/QA F1-like metrics or <=2.0% relative perplexity increase for LM-style tasks, otherwise reject profile
Runtime enforces guardrail: if production inference observes accuracy regressions > acceptance thresholds or OOMs, traffic auto-rolls back to FP16 variant and creates an incident with diagnostics
Console UI surfaces recommended profile, expected latency/cost delta, and a link to the detailed calibration report for each model version
CI gate refuses merging a model_catalog update that introduces a new default profile without an attached calibration artifact and validation report
Documentation page explaining calibration steps, sample datasets, and recommended dataset sizes updated and linked from the catalog entry
notes: Primary focus: balance production economics (cost/latency) with predictable output quality. We prefer conservative defaults for customer-facing LLMs and more aggressive defaults for closed-loop batch workloads.

We will treat FP8 as the recommended default for transformer encoder-decoder and decoder-only models where calibration shows <1% abs quality drop and stable activation distributions during runtime traces.
INT8 static will be recommended for smaller, well-tested models or for customers on Dedicated where memory savings are paramount and we can enforce stricter calibration data requirements.

Fallback semantics: runtime supports explicit model_variant aliases: model@fp8, model@int8, model@fp16. Default points to model@<quant_default>. Runtime can transparently fallback to model@fp16 on policy triggers.

Calibration dataset guidance: minimum 2k representative sequences for language generation tasks, 5k for open-vocab classification; sample slicing should include long-tail prompts used in production (prefixes, few-shot contexts).

Validation metrics: task-specific metric (accuracy/F1/ROUGE) plus LM metrics (perplexity) when relevant, plus latency and memory footprint. Each calibration run must publish these numbers and a 95% confidence interval computed via bootstrapping.
comments: 2026-03-01 Avery Kim: Initial spike complete. Wireframe for catalog UI and calibration artifact schema posted to Confluence. Decided to store calibration artifacts under s3://redwood-quant/calibrations.

2026-03-03 Diego Martins: Implemented prototype calibration runner that collects activation histograms, per-layer clipping thresholds, and a validation harness that runs evaluation tasks in parallel. Most models finish within 45-70 minutes on m5-large runner with 4 GPUs.

2026-03-05 Priya Shah (PM): Reviewed acceptance criteria. Requested stricter default for public hosted models — require <=0.5% absolute delta for chat/QA top-tier hosted models. Added to safety matrix.

2026-03-07 Design feedback (Maya Ortiz): Catalog page should show delta visualization (bar chart) with clear color bands for safe / marginal / reject. Also suggested inline link to playback traces that produced worst-case activation samples.

2026-03-09 Security (J. Patel): Confirmed that calibration artifacts do not contain customer prompt data. Calibration harness must accept only synthetic/owned prompt sets or customer-provided consented data. Marked security_review_required=false but requires checklist entry in runbook.

2026-03-10 Diego Martins: Pushed RFC with the safety matrix and CI gating rules. Requesting eng review before merging into model-catalog schema PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/model-catalog/pull/482
benchmarks: fp8 (recommended) avg latency reduction: 22% (95th perc: 18-27%) vs fp16 on p4d, cost reduction: ~28%
int8 (static) median latency reduction: 35% vs fp16 for small-batch throughput workloads, but observed quality volatility on long-context prompts for 2 of 15 models tested

Observed worst-case quality delta across full suite: 1.9% abs on a noisy summarization task when using naive per-layer minmax clipping; improved to 0.6% after percentile clipping + per-channel scaling
